body:
_Original comment by_ **BitBucket: [dmand](http://bitbucket.org/dmand), GitHub: @dmand?**:

---

About your first case.

Right now checker skips `not-an-iterable` and `unsupported-membership-test` checks for statements that are inside mixin classes (classes that have 'mixin' at the end of their names). So if you rename `BaseType` to `BaseMixin` - the error should not be emitted.

Maybe we should skip checks not only for mixins, but for `AbstractXXX` and `BaseYYY` classes too.

_Original comment by_ **Florian Bruhin (BitBucket: [The-Compiler](http://bitbucket.org/The-Compiler), GitHub: @The-Compiler?)**:

---

Sounds like a good idea, IMHO - for the second case, I guess renaming that class to `AbstractUrlMarkManager` or so would make more sense anyways.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

Disabling these messages for abstract classes sounds good to me. This means a soft name check (does it contain 'Abstract') and also a hard check (is it truly abstract, does it export abstract methods?) In other classes, the errors won't probably be triggered when we'll have flow control analysis, but it's not going to happen in the next month for sure. I'm not saying that it's not common, but the same issues can also occur with no-member or other similar messages, prone to false positives due to the flow sensitivity of the analysis.

_Original comment by_ **BitBucket: [dmand](http://bitbucket.org/dmand), GitHub: @dmand?**:

---

I think that checker for abstract classes (hard check) should probably be separated from checker for iterables. And checker for iterables should just use soft check to assume that class is abstract.

_Original comment by_ **Claudiu Popa (BitBucket: [PCManticore](http://bitbucket.org/PCManticore), GitHub: @PCManticore)**:

---

Skip not-an-iterable and similar checks for Base/Abstract classes

And refactor iterable checker.

Fixes issue #685.
